title: Co-pilot draft stayed startable while a produce ran (one side of the guard)
body:
## Summary
useProduce blocked Produce during a co-pilot draft, but Draft with Claude and the follow-up Send stayed live during a produce.

## Description
The rule 'a draft and a produce never overlap' had one implementation: apps/studio/src/studio/shared.tsx useProduce (`!llm` in canProduce). apps/studio/src/studio/Copilot.tsx disabled Draft only on `start.isPending || running` (llm job). The produce chain reads the latest props at each step (apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:258 renderJob reads latestProps and throws 'no timing: generate audio first'), and ProjectService.setProps stores a new version without timing (apps/server/src/projects.ts:109-110), so a draft that stores props between the audio and the render job fails the render. Fixed: draftBlockReason (apps/studio/src/studio/copilot-log.ts) disables Draft and Send with the reason shown; the follow-up input stays editable.

## Flow
- owner presses Produce -> audio job runs
- owner presses Draft with Claude (still enabled) -> co-pilot calls set_props -> props v(n+1) without timing
- audio ends, enqueues render -> renderJob reads v(n+1) -> throws 'no timing: generate audio first'

## Expected impact
The owner can no longer start a draft that breaks the produce in flight; the reason is on screen. Nothing else changes: drafting is enabled again the moment the chain ends.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the overlap rule is enforced on both sides in the UI
Before: 0 of 2 draftBlockReason cases pass; guard on 1 of 2 sides
After: 2 of 2 pass; guard on 2 of 2 sides
Method: gate - copilot-log.test.ts red (helper absent) then green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: apps/studio/src/studio/shared.tsx:187 canProduce (before: included !llm); apps/studio/src/studio/copilot-log.ts:94 draftBlockReason; apps/studio/src/studio/Copilot.tsx:116 (before) disabled={start.isPending || running}; apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:258-261; apps/server/src/projects.ts:109-110; commit e07ee8e

title: Produce disabled by a running co-pilot draft showed no reason
body:
## Summary
A co-pilot draft disabled Produce with no hint and no title; blockReason only knew the unbuilt-composition case.

## Description
apps/studio/src/studio/shared.tsx useProduce computed `blockReason = produceBlockReason(compositionState(...))` and folded `!llm` into canProduce separately, so the control room's stage bar (which renders blockReason as a hint and title) showed a dead Produce with nothing said. produceBlockReason (apps/studio/src/studio-logic.ts) now takes the drafting flag and names it; canProduce reads the reason. Registry: async-ui-states / action-busy-states (a disabled control says why).

## Flow
- co-pilot drafting -> Produce disabled
- stage bar: no hint, button has no title
- after: 'The co-pilot is drafting; Produce once the draft ends.'

## Expected impact
The owner sees why Produce is greyed out. Could break: nothing; the composition reason still wins.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every disabled Produce cause beyond missing props/script carries text
Before: disabled-without-reason causes: 1 (co-pilot drafting); 0 of 3 new test cases pass
After: 0; 3 of 3 pass
Method: gate - studio-logic.test.ts red then green
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Props JSON editor discarded unsaved edits when the co-pilot stored props
body:
## Summary
JsonEdit was keyed on detail.props.version, so a new props version remounted it and silently dropped the owner's typing.

## Description
apps/studio/src/studio/PropsPanel.tsx rendered `<JsonEdit key={detail.props?.version ?? 0} .../>`; any set_props from a running co-pilot draft (or another tab) bumped the version and remounted the editor with the stored text. Registry: draft-editing / draft-model (the baseline advances only by the owner's own save; edits are never replaced by a refetch). Fixed: rebasePropsDraft (apps/studio/src/studio-logic.ts) lets an untouched draft follow new props, keeps an edited one, and the editor states which version landed underneath (Save supersedes it, Reset loads it).

## Flow
- owner opens JSON, edits rows
- co-pilot (still drafting) calls set_props -> v+1
- before: editor remounts, edits gone; after: edits kept, notice 'Props v.. were stored while you edited v..'

## Expected impact
No more silent loss of hand edits during a draft. Could break: an untouched editor still follows; timing-only updates (attachTiming keeps the version) behave as before.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - unsaved JSON edits survive a new props version
Before: edits lost on a new version: 1 of 1 (key remount); 0 of 3 rebasePropsDraft cases pass
After: edits lost: 0; 3 of 3 pass
Method: gate - studio-logic.test.ts red then green; wiring by probe (key removed, draft state rebased)
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A failed composition chunk load was cached until a full reload
body:
## Summary
loadComposition kept a rejected import as {status: missing} in its ??= cache, so the monitor stayed 'unavailable' for the life of the tab.

## Description
apps/studio/src/composition.ts cached `import("@statreel/compositions")` with ??= and resolved a failure into a 'missing' info that every later call returned. A dev-server restart or a build error being fixed left the player and the tracks ruler ('The composition could not be loaded') dead until reload. Fixed: the failure handler clears the cache; a good chunk is still loaded once.

## Flow
- compositions chunk fails once
- owner fixes it, navigates away and back
- before: still unavailable; after: loads

## Expected impact
The monitor recovers on the next mount. Could break: nothing; success path unchanged (pinned by test).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a transient chunk failure is not permanent
Before: 1 of 2 cases pass (retry after failure stays 'missing')
After: 2 of 2
Method: gate - new apps/studio/src/composition.test.ts (vi.doMock failing then working module) red then green
Result: better
Gate: none

body:

## Description

- select A in the picker

The status matches the transcript on screen. Could break: nothing; DRAFTING/QUEUED still read the live job.

## Evaluation

Before: 0 of 2 sessionJob cases pass; chip for failed older session = DONE
After: 2 of 2; chip = FAILED

title: Produce stepper marks were a hand copy of pipeline.ts with no derived test

## Evaluation

Before: tests reading the producer: 0
After: 2; seeded CHECKS_AT 0.92 -> 0.95 turned 3 red, restored green
Method: gate - seeded violation
Result: better

title: Gate page checks table disagrees with the OPA gate on duration and black frames
body:
## Summary
The Duration row is judged against the use case's band (45-75 s for era-adjusted) while the gate denies outside 30-90 s; black frames have no target though the gate denies > 1 s.

## Description
apps/studio/src/studio/RenderGatePage.tsx:31 passes `usecase?.duration_s` to checkRows (apps/studio/src/logic.ts:376-382), so a 35 s or 80 s render shows Duration FAIL next to an ALLOW verdict; policy/publish.rego:71 holds the gate's band {30, 90} and :74 max_black_s 1, which checkRows never shows (black_frames_s target null, 'recorded'). The deny hint (apps/studio/src/studio/deny-hints.ts) states 30-90 s. Registry: quality-gates / policy-projection - a dashboard that disagrees with the gate. Fix: rows carry the gate's own thresholds (projected from the policy, e.g. via the policy verdict or a shared constant pinned by a test that reads the rego) and label the use-case band as an editorial target, not a pass/fail.

## Flow
- render an era-adjusted video of 80 s
- gate: ALLOW; checks table: Duration 80 s, target 45-75 s, FAIL
- render with 1.5 s of black: gate DENY 'black frames longer than 1 s'; table row says 'recorded'

## Expected impact
The owner stops seeing a FAIL the gate does not enforce, and sees the black-frame threshold the gate does. Could break: the editorial band disappears unless kept as a separate label.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - table verdicts equal gate verdicts
Before: rules where table and gate disagree: 2 of the 7 thresholded rows (duration, black frames)
After: 0 (predicted)
Method: simulation - three cases walked (80 s ALLOW/FAIL, 35 s ALLOW/FAIL, 1.5 s black DENY/recorded); a gate test needs logic.ts, outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: logic.test.ts case reading policy/publish.rego duration_band_s/max_black_s and asserting checkRows rows' ok equals the gate's; seed 80 s -> red today
note: out-of-scope (logic.ts = Studio Shell & Data Layer); RenderGatePage.tsx reserved by cards session - wait

title: Schedule in Calendar is offered while the project already has a calendar slot
body:
## Summary
scheduleOffered counts publications only; the Calendar refuses a second slot ('this project is already on the calendar').

## Description
apps/studio/src/studio-logic.ts:128-132 scheduleOffered = gate allows && idle && publications.length === 0. A scheduled-but-not-yet-published slot is a schedule row, not a publication (apps/server/src/calendar.ts:138 refuses a second slot for the project), and ProjectDetail (apps/server/src/app.ts:132-145) carries no slot, so both compose screens keep offering 'Schedule in Calendar' and the stage bar says 'Schedule it' for a project that is already scheduled. Fix: ProjectDetail gains the project's live slot; scheduleOffered takes it; the stage bar shows the slot instead.

- back to the control room: 'Schedule in Calendar' still offered
- Calendar: 'this project is already on the calendar'

Before: offer shown while a slot exists: yes (1 of 1 walked case)
After: no (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked from calendar.ts:132-147 and studio-logic.ts:121; needs a server field (app.ts) outside this round's paths
Result: better

title: Timeline drag-scrub keeps seeking after a release outside the window
body:
## Summary
Tracks seekFrom listens on window pointermove/pointerup without pointer capture or pointercancel.

## Description
apps/studio/src/studio/Tracks.tsx:91-107 adds window listeners on pointerdown and removes them only on pointerup. A release outside the browser window (or a touch pointercancel) never reaches pointerup, so the next hover over the page keeps moving the playhead with no button pressed until some click. Registry: media-playback / playback-clock (needle snaps under a scrub). Fix: setPointerCapture on the lane and end on pointerup/pointercancel/lostpointercapture, or end when ev.buttons === 0.

## Flow
- press on the Scenes lane, drag past the window edge, release outside
- move the mouse back over the page: playhead follows

## Expected impact
No phantom scrubbing. Could break: drag feel if capture is mis-set.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a scrub ends when the pointer is released
Before: release paths that end the scrub: 1 of 3 (pointerup inside; not outside, not cancel)
After: 3 of 3 (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked from the listener code; no browser driver in this round (Playwright is director-only)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Playwright: pointerdown on .tl-ruler, mouse.up outside the viewport, mouse.move inside, assert the player frame does not change

title: sceneSpans promises missing scenes keep their draft place; the code drops them
body:
## Summary
The docstring says scenes missing from the timing keep their draft place so none disappears; only timed scenes are returned.

## Description
apps/studio/src/studio-logic.ts:25-46: the loop pushes a span only when the timing has the scene. A props scene absent from timing (props JSON saved with a new scene and the old timing block, which set_props accepts - packages/schemas/src/index.ts:147 timing optional, no scene cross-check) vanishes from the ruler and the script modal says 'no time yet'. Either the comment or the code is wrong; which one depends on what the composition plays for that scene.

## Flow
- add a scene in the props JSON, keep timing, Save
- Tracks: the new scene is not on the ruler; the docstring says it would be

## Expected impact
The ruler (or its doc) tells the truth about untimed scenes. Could break: span layout if a draft place overlaps measured spans.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - doc and code agree, ruler shows every scene the composition plays
Before: scenes missing from timing shown: 0 of 1 (doc claims 1 of 1)
After: agreement either way (needs the composition's behaviour)
Method: simulation - walked sceneSpans with one extra scene; a test can pin it once the intended behaviour is chosen
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: studio-logic.test case: sceneSpans(scenes + 'extra', timing) and the composition's timing resolver on the same props

title: The props JSON editor round-trips the stored timing block into new props
body:
## Summary
JsonEdit pre-fills JSON.stringify(props) including timing, so a hand edit to scenes saves a timing that no longer matches them.

## Description
apps/studio/src/studio/PropsPanel.tsx JsonEdit builds its text from detail.props.props, which carries the audio stage's timing (words, cues, music); ProjectService.setProps stores whatever validates (apps/server/src/projects.ts:102-112) and the schema does not cross-check timing against scenes. Editing a scene's text or order in JSON yields a props version whose timing describes the old scenes - the preview plays stale cues until the next Produce. Fix: edit without timing (strip on open, server keeps or drops timing explicitly).

## Flow
- after a Produce, open JSON, reorder two scenes, Save
- preview and ruler use the old timing for the new order

## Expected impact
Hand edits never carry a timing that lies about the scenes. Could break: owners who relied on keeping timing across a cosmetic edit.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - stored timing always matches stored scenes
Before: JSON edit preserves stale timing: yes
After: no (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked from PropsPanel JsonEdit and projects.ts setProps; the store-side fix is server code
Result: better
Gate: contract
instrument: server test: setProps with scenes not covered by timing is refused or stored without timing

title: The draft/produce overlap rule exists only in the browser
body:

apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:106-108 produce enqueues unconditionally and apps/server/src/llm-service.ts:125-147 start has no produce check; the job runner serialises per kind only (apps/server/src/jobs.ts:2). title: Co-pilot composer cannot take a follow-up while a turn runs
body:
## Summary
The follow-up input is disabled for the whole draft, so a thought typed mid-answer has nowhere to go.

## Description

Registry: chat-transcript / composer-turn-queue ('the send control is disabled while a turn runs; a user types a follow-up mid-answer and loses it') - the standard keeps typing open and queues the turn. Queuing follow-ups is a capability the context does not declare.

## Flow
- Draft with Claude runs
- owner wants to add 'use 2010-2020 only'
- input disabled until the draft ends

## Expected impact
The owner can steer without waiting. Could break: the CLI session model (one resume at a time).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - follow-ups can be composed and queued during a turn
Before: follow-up composable while running: no
After: unmeasurable until the queue semantics are chosen
Method: simulation - registry deviation; queueing is a product decision
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
